title: Solutions to the Einstein-scalar-field system in spherical symmetry with large bounded variation norms (arXiv v1 e-print TeX)
authors: Jonathan Luk, Sung-Jin Oh, Shiwu Yang
exact_version: arXiv:1605.03893v1, submitted 12 May 2016; e-print file SSESF-LargeBVScat.160512.tex (sha-checkable at source; 3214 lines)
relevance: Primary source for the entire finite-control chain: Theorem 1.1 (existence/uniqueness/completeness, (1.7)-(1.9), Remark 1.2), Definition 2.1 C^k class, (2.4)-(2.5) data/gauge, (2.6)/(2.8)/(2.10)-(2.11) reduced equations, Lemma 3.1, Prop 3.3, Prop 3.4 (3.16)-(3.18), Prop 3.8 (3.25), Prop 3.18 (3.44)-(3.47), Section 4 compactness and (4.1) plus the two unnumbered remainder displays, Section 6 geodesic completeness with the 'completely identical' past-half sentence.
limits: Selected loci read at full-text depth from the downloaded v1 TeX (not a cover-to-cover audit). Confirmed verbatim: Remark 1.2 u0-independence; Prop 3.18 constants independent of u0,v0,A; Section 4 order of limits 'n to infinity first and then u to -infinity'; the Section 4 r-derivative display k=0 term is a confirmed typo (claims |d_v r|+|d_u r| <= eps(A+eps), impossible since lambda ~ 1/2); the convergence display's leading phi must be read as phi^(n); Prop 3.18 u-side halves are an explicit sketch ('we only sketch the argument'); local well-posedness/uniqueness proof is OMITTED ('easy to show', 'We omit the proof, which is a routine iteration argument'); Section 6 past completeness is one sentence. Mixed third derivatives are asserted in one line ('follow from the wave equations'), not proved. Numbering cross-checked against the arXiv HTML rendering of v1 (Prop 3.18 = higher-derivative proposition; thm:main = Theorem 1.7; (4.1) = the incoming-limit claim).
assumptions: (1.7): int_u^v |Phi| <= eps (v-u)^{1-deltac}, |Phi|+|Phi'| <= eps for all v>=u>=u0; smooth Phi; for Theorem 1.7 additionally sup|Phi''| < infinity on all of R.
conclusion: Unique global C^k (k>=1, Definition 2.1) characteristic solution, future causally geodesically complete, with uniform a priori bounds (1.8)-(1.9); Section 4 limit recovers lim lambda = 1/2 and lim lambda^{-1} d_v(r phi) = Phi with the two remainder displays.
proof_status: Printed for the a priori estimates and compactness; uniqueness and local well-posedness asserted with proof omitted; higher-order u-side halves sketched.
open_questions: Does the published Ann. PDE 4(1):3 (2018) version print the uniqueness argument and full u-side Prop 3.18 proofs? Do the estimates' constants depend on data only through (deltac, eps, A) locus by locus (checked for the consumed displays; full sweep open).

title: Timelike completeness as an obstruction to C^0-extensions
authors: Gregory J. Galloway, Eric Ling, Jan Sbierski
exact_version: arXiv:1704.00353v4 HTML read for abstract and Theorem 1 statement, 2026-10-30
relevance: External input cited by SMOOTH_FINITE_CONTROL.md sec 2 for C^0-inextendibility. Theorem 1 verbatim: 'A smooth (at least C^2) time-oriented Lorentzian manifold that is timelike geodesically complete and globally hyperbolic is C^0-inextendible.'
limits: Abstract and Theorem 1 statement read; proof not read. The 'at least C^2' hypothesis is real and load-bearing for the separation of categories: it does NOT apply to the bare C^{1,1} model of C11_FINITE_CONTROL.md, so that model has the section 7 Cauchy-slice property but no C^0-inextendibility from this source.
